description: Camera: give ChaseCamera a reverse case and make mouse look frame-rate independent (brief Tasks 1 and 2). Both defects live in the same file and the same per-frame pipeline, so they ship together. Reversing today points the view at a spot cameraLookAhead metres in FRONT of the car (28 m on Tuning_Balanced, 34 m on Tuning_Loose) while the car travels backwards at up to reverseTopSpeed 8 m/s, and ComputeHeading's Vector3.Slerp(nose, velocity.normalized, 0.25) is ill-conditioned once reverse speed passes the existing 1.5 m/s gate because nose and velocity are then antiparallel and Slerp has no defined axis between opposite vectors. Separately, ReadSwivelInput multiplies the mouse delta by Time.deltaTime, which is backwards for a displacement: 0.06 (the ScaleVector2 processor on <Mouse>/delta) x 120 (cameraSwivelSpeed) x dt gives 0.24 deg/px at 30 fps, 0.12 at 60 and 0.05 at 144. Independent of FEAT-002 and FEAT-003; ordered first because it is the highest-value fix. Execution is sequential regardless.

Read plan.md items 2, 3 and 4 in full. They carry the exact field names, defaults, tooltip content and formulae; implement them as written rather than re-deriving.

In Assets/Project/Scripts/Vehicle/VehicleInput.cs, add `public bool CameraLookIsMouse { get; private set; } = true;` with an XML doc saying why the camera needs it (mouse delta is a displacement, stick is a rate), and set it in Update right after `CameraLook = look;`: when `_cameraLook != null && look.sqrMagnitude > 0f`, read `_cameraLook.activeControl?.device` and, if non-null, assign `device is Mouse`. Sticky on purpose: activeControl is null at rest. `using UnityEngine.InputSystem;` is already there.

In Assets/Project/Scripts/Vehicle/ChaseCamera.cs add a [Header("Reverse view")] block after collisionLayers with five [Tooltip]+[SerializeField] private floats: reverseViewEnterSpeed -1.5, reverseViewExitSpeed -0.5, reverseViewHoldTime 0.25, reverseViewTransitionTime 0.45, reverseViewReturnDelay 0.35. Tooltip wording is in plan.md item 2; it must name the precedents (-1.5 matches ComputeHeading's own velocity gate, -0.5 matches the controller's reverse gate, and cameraSwivelRecentreDelay 1.2 s is the file's existing timing precedent).

Add a [Header("Mouse look")] block with mouseLookDegreesPerPixel 0.05 and mouseLookDeadzonePixels 1, plus `private const float MouseBindingDeltaScale = 0.06f;` commented as the ScaleVector2 processor on <Mouse>/delta in VehicleControls.inputactions and in VehicleInput.BuildFallbackControls.

Add private state next to _yawOffset: _reverseBlend, _reverseTarget, _reverseHold, _forwardHold. Write UpdateReverseView(float dt) exactly as in plan.md item 2: below enter speed accumulate _reverseHold and set target 1 after reverseViewHoldTime; at or above exit speed accumulate _forwardHold and set target 0 after reverseViewReturnDelay; between them (the dead zone) change nothing; then Mathf.MoveTowards the blend toward the target at dt / reverseViewTransitionTime so a full swing takes exactly that long.

Write ApplyReverseView(Vector3 heading): return the heading unchanged when the eased blend is ~0, otherwise `Quaternion.AngleAxis(180f * Mathf.SmoothStep(0f, 1f, _reverseBlend), Vector3.up) * heading`. Comment WHY a single rotation about world up rather than negating the look-ahead (that would put the aim point behind the camera and lose the car from frame) or lerping the signs (that walks the camera through the car).

Rewire LateUpdate: keep ComputeHeading and the existing SmoothDirection on _smoothedHeading (so _smoothedHeading stays in nose space and its own Slerp never sees a large step), then call UpdateReverseView(dt), then `Vector3 viewHeading = ApplyReverseView(_smoothedHeading);` and pass viewHeading to ComputeDesiredPosition, KeepOutOfWalls and ComputeDesiredRotation instead of _smoothedHeading.

Guard ComputeHeading: after the existing `velocity.magnitude < 1.5f` gate, compute `Vector3 velocityDirection = velocity.normalized;` and return ApplySwivel(nose) when `Vector3.Dot(nose, velocityDirection) <= -0.95f` (about 162 degrees), with a named const and a comment that Slerp has no defined axis between opposite vectors and that driftSlipAngleThreshold is 12 degrees so no normal slide is affected. Keep the existing blend for every other case.

Reset the new reverse state in SnapToTarget next to `_yawOffset = 0f` (blend, target and both timers to 0) and build its pose from ApplyReverseView(_smoothedHeading). VehicleMeasurement.ResetCar calls SnapToTarget before every reading (VehicleMeasurement.cs:1016-1017), so without this a reading after a reversing run starts half swung round.
In DrawSightlineGizmos, when Application.isPlaying, draw the sightline along the reverse-rotated heading so the gizmo matches what the camera is doing.

Rewrite ReadSwivelInput as two branches sharing one idle/recentre tail. Mouse branch (input.CameraLookIsMouse, or input == null / device unknown): `Vector2 pixels = look / MouseBindingDeltaScale;` ignore when `pixels.magnitude < mouseLookDeadzonePixels`, otherwise add `pixels.x * mouseLookDegreesPerPixel` to _yawOffset and subtract `pixels.y * mouseLookDegreesPerPixel` from _pitchOffset inside the existing Mathf.Clamp(-35f, 55f), with NO Time.deltaTime. Stick branch: the current `look.x * Tuning.cameraSwivelSpeed * dt` arithmetic and the current `look.sqrMagnitude > 0.0001f` gate, unchanged. The idle tail (_timeSinceSwivel += dt and the cameraSwivelRecentreDelay recentre) must behave exactly as it does today.
Update the class-level XML doc: the camera now has a reverse case, and the two devices are scaled differently on purpose. Keep the file's existing voice.

Run the verification commands. Record in findings: the before/after degrees-per-pixel table at 30, 60 and 144 fps recomputed from the shipped values (0.06 x 120 x dt before; mouseLookDegreesPerPixel after, frame-rate independent), and the exact compile_check and pytest output.

Commit locally on fix/reverse-and-recovery with a subject <= 72 chars and a body saying why (GIT-RULES rule 3). Check `git diff --cached --name-only` first: only the two source files, never a csproj, never PlaytestLogs/.
Set this feature's status to completed in FEAT-001.json and write findings, including the play-test items from plan.md item 5 that cannot be settled without Unity.

MOUSE LOOK SENSITIVITY, BEFORE vs AFTER, recomputed from the values actually shipped. Before: degrees per pixel = MouseBindingDeltaScale 0.06 (the ScaleVector2 processor on <Mouse>/delta) x cameraSwivelSpeed 120 (identical on all three Tuning profiles) x dt = 7.2 x dt. After: mouseLookDegreesPerPixel 0.05, with no dt anywhere on the mouse path.
  30 fps  (dt 0.0333): before 0.24 deg/px -> after 0.05 deg/px (4.8x slower)
  60 fps  (dt 0.0167): before 0.12 deg/px -> after 0.05 deg/px (2.4x slower)
  144 fps (dt 0.00694): before 0.050 deg/px -> after 0.05 deg/px (unchanged, by design: the fastest machine is the one that already felt right)
  A 400 px sweep at 60 fps: 48 deg before, 20 deg after. The same sweep now yields 20 deg at 30, 60 and 144 fps; before it yielded 96 / 48 / 20 deg.
  Dead zone: the old gate was look.sqrMagnitude > 0.0001 on the already-scaled vector, i.e. 0.01/0.06 = 0.167 px, which a resting hand clears and which also kept restarting cameraSwivelRecentreDelay so the camera never auto-recentred. Now mouseLookDeadzonePixels = 1 px.
  Gamepad is untouched: the stick branch still reads look.x * Tuning.cameraSwivelSpeed * dt behind the original look.sqrMagnitude > 0.0001f gate, and no tuning value was read differently or written.

WHAT WAS IMPLEMENTED. ChaseCamera gained a [Header("Reverse view")] block (reverseViewEnterSpeed -1.5, reverseViewExitSpeed -0.5, reverseViewHoldTime 0.25, reverseViewTransitionTime 0.45, reverseViewReturnDelay 0.35) and a [Header("Mouse look")] block (mouseLookDegreesPerPixel 0.05, mouseLookDeadzonePixels 1), all seven [Tooltip] + [SerializeField] private floats on the MonoBehaviour, so they tune in the inspector with no recompile and need no scene edit (a scene saved before the fields existed carries no entry for them, so Unity falls back to the C# initialisers). UpdateReverseView(dt) runs the hold/dead-zone/return-delay state machine and Mathf.MoveTowards the blend at dt / reverseViewTransitionTime; ApplyReverseView rotates the heading by 180 x Mathf.SmoothStep(0,1,blend) about Vector3.up. LateUpdate keeps ComputeHeading + SmoothDirection on _smoothedHeading (so that Slerp stays in nose space and never sees a 180 deg step) and then passes the rotated viewHeading to ComputeDesiredPosition / KeepOutOfWalls / ComputeDesiredRotation. ComputeHeading returns ApplySwivel(nose) when Vector3.Dot(nose, velocity.normalized) <= -0.95 (about 162 deg; driftSlipAngleThreshold is 12 deg so no slide is affected). SnapToTarget resets _reverseBlend/_reverseTarget/_reverseHold/_forwardHold and builds its pose from ApplyReverseView(_smoothedHeading), which matters because VehicleMeasurement.ResetCar calls SnapToTarget before every reading (VehicleMeasurement.cs:1016-1017). DrawSightlineGizmos uses the reverse-rotated heading while Application.isPlaying. VehicleInput gained `public bool CameraLookIsMouse { get; private set; } = true;` set in Update right after `CameraLook = look;` from `_cameraLook.activeControl?.device is Mouse`, only while look.sqrMagnitude > 0 and only when the device is non-null, so it is deliberately sticky (activeControl is null at rest) and defaults to mouse when unknown. No new input action, so the README Controls table and VehicleControls.inputactions are both unchanged and test_readme_controls_have_required_actions_and_bindings still passes.

CAMERA FEEL: PLAY TEST ONLY, NOT SETTLEABLE STATICALLY. None of the following can be judged from the code or the tooling; all seven numbers are serialized, so tuning any of them needs no recompile. Open Assets/Project/Scenes/Possible game scene.unity in Unity 6000.5.4f1 and:
  1. Hold S past -1.5 m/s and confirm the camera swings round ONCE, eased rather than lurching, and that 0.45 s reads as a swing and not a whip. The ease shape is SmoothStep over a MoveTowards, so the swing is slowest at both ends.
  2. Brake to a full stop with Left Ctrl and confirm the camera does NOT swing. This is the -1.5/-0.5 dead zone plus the 0.25 s hold doing its job; if it still twitches, raise reverseViewHoldTime before touching the speeds.
  3. Shuffle forward and back through a three point turn and confirm the camera swings at most once, not twice per shuffle. That is reverseViewReturnDelay 0.35; whether 1 m/s of dead band is wide enough for a real three point turn is exactly the open question.
  4. Sweep the mouse with vsync on and off (and with a frame cap at 30 if available) and confirm the camera turns the same amount for the same hand movement. Also confirm 0.05 deg/px does not feel sluggish to the tester, because it is 2.4x slower than the 60 fps feel they have been playing with; if it does, raise mouseLookDegreesPerPixel rather than reintroducing dt.
  5. Confirm a resting hand now lets the camera auto-recentre after cameraSwivelRecentreDelay 1.2 s (the 1 px dead zone is what makes that possible) and that 1 px does not feel sticky when starting a slow pan.
  6. Reverse fast (up to reverseTopSpeed 8 m/s) along a street and confirm the camera is not clipping into buildings as it comes round the side of the car: KeepOutOfWalls runs on the rotated heading, so it should pull in correctly, but the swing path past the car's flank has never been seen against real geometry.
  7. Plug in a gamepad and confirm the right stick behaves exactly as before, which also confirms CameraLookIsMouse is flipping as intended.
  8. Run the F5 road-ahead measurement in VehicleLab after a reversing run and confirm the reading is normal, which confirms the SnapToTarget reset.
